senses.definition: something such as an attitude or rule that stops people from communicating, understanding each other, or making progress

examples.en: A wall of silence prevented them from finding the truth.

senses.definition: a page or section on a social media website where users share public messages, pictures, or comments

senses.definition: a row of players standing side by side to defend their goal during a free kick in football

senses.definition: a thick mass of people, objects, or substances that stands together and blocks movement or view

blocks.etymology: From Middle English wal, from Old English weall (“wall, dike, earthwork, rampart, dam, rocky shore, cliff”), from Proto-West Germanic *wall (“wall, rampart, entrenchment”), from Latin vallum (“wall, rampart, entrenchment, palisade”), from Proto-Indo-European *welH- (“to turn, wind, roll”). Perhaps conflated with waw (“a wall within a house or dwelling, a room partition”), from Middle English wawe, from Old English wāg, wāh (“an interior wall, divider”), see waw.
